findings.text: follow-on: _aggregate_rows already keys a parsed crew document (crew.json) on the same four-field stat identity the new ledger.document_identity recomputes, so the repository now holds two private stat-identity document caches in one write scope that can drift; the general memoised reader is a legitimate new capability, so this is a helper duplication rather than a forked owner and it does not hold the node.

follow-on: _DOCUMENT_CACHE is process-lifetime and drops an entry only when a later read is attempted after its file is gone, so a long-lived producer that watches run files appear and then be deleted or renamed retains every document it ever parsed, leaving the memo uncapped across the producer's life.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base c8911c29; 4eaa7422d adds the memoised reader and switches both callers, and 7107fe5f1 only re-annotates the counter's __enter__ return as Self, changing no behaviour.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_a_sweep_decodes_each_document_once.py building at least 200 per-run files and 20 live pointers and counting json.loads across one sweep; logs/head-gate.log records "7 passed in 21.64s" EXIT=0 for that test plus test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py, and negative-control/base-tree-count.log records the base arm failing the first count with "a sweep decoded 400 run documents from 200 files", EXIT=1.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that one obligation sweep decode each crew document at most once and a later sweep skip documents whose stat identity is unchanged; the diff routes the per-run read in reckon/crew/obligations.py:431 (_run_file_record) and reckon/ledger.py:1121 (_read_run) through the stat-identity-keyed memo at reckon/ledger.py:1104, so one sweep's two readers of each run file share a single parse.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names commits 4eaa7422d and 7107fe5f1, the head arm "7 passed in 21.64s" EXIT=0, the base-tree negative control "3 failed in 22.75s" EXIT=1, and it discloses under follow_ons that live-pointer documents, mounts.json and the ledger index payloads remain multi-decoded outside the fence.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares reckon/crew/obligations.py, reckon/ledger.py, reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py, the test file and the evidence fragment; git diff c8911c29..7107fe5f1 touches only obligations.py, ledger.py, the test file and the fragment, all inside the declared set, with recovery_classification.py declared but untouched.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_sweep_decodes_each_document_once.py:168 fails if any run file is decoded twice (the base arm reddens at "assert 400 <= 200"), :186 fails unless a later sweep decodes exactly the one changed file (the base arm reddens at 201), and :204 fails if the memo changes the written snapshot.
justifications.evidence: the pytest arm of the done_when is recorded in logs/head-gate.log ("7 passed in 21.64s", EXIT=0) and negative-control/base-tree-count.log (EXIT=1), but the done_when's ruff arm is claimed only by commit 7107fe5f1 and no ruff log is recorded.
justifications.fit: reckon/ledger.py:1104 follows the module's private-helper and module-global memo idiom and the added names read_document, document_identity and _DOCUMENT_CACHE carry no plan or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/ledger.py:1104 holds each decoded document against its (st_dev, st_ino, st_size, st_mtime_ns) identity, and corroborating negative-control/base-tree-count.log shows the sweep's two readers no longer decode a run file twice (400 decodes fall to 200).
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/obligations.py:459 _aggregate_rows already owns a parse-once-per-stat-identity cache of a crew document and computes the identical (st_dev, st_ino, st_size, st_mtime_ns) key at reckon/crew/obligations.py:466, so reckon/ledger.py:1095 document_identity restates that identity rather than sharing one owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in git diff c8911c29..7107fe5f1 is inside the write paths declared in the manifest, and recovery_classification.py is declared but not touched, so nothing out of scope is carried.
